tasks.short: Show the person how to use the equipment or do the routine.

steps.what: Read this person's limits from the clinical record {OTHER}
Choose which routines fit the limits she just read
Demonstrate correct use of exercise equipment or performance of exercise routines

tasks.design: Nothing is built. She reads limits in the clinical record {OTHER}, chooses the routine, and demonstrates it in the room. No work is removed. A save of the same record is not a second entry, and the demonstration is spoken, so there is no transport to drop. The session is not recorded.
tasks.previous_blocker: The correct routine depends on this person's limits and on watching their form.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes the demonstration. The limits are already in the clinical record.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing an unsafe joint angle and changing the routine in the moment.
tasks.human_edge: She can feel when a person is about to compensate and stop the set.
tasks.altitude: Her week still holds the limit check, the routine choice, and the live demonstration. Nothing in this task is removed.

reach.task: Show a home exercise the person will repeat alone
reach.learn: Which spoken cues a therapist uses when she cannot stand beside the person.

evidence.claim: A live demonstration of equipment or a routine is not a consultation note, so note-writing time cuts do not apply to this task.
Works-council consent applies to ambient recording of how staff work. This design records nothing.

assumptions: The focal role is the exercise physiologist. The workflow boundary is this demonstration: read the limits, choose the routine, show it. No other role's hours are in the baseline.
No structured input is produced for a machine. There is no machine step.
No work is removed. There is no second entry and no transport. A save of the clinical record {OTHER} is the same record she already read.

Participants are patients, outside the organisation, so the demonstration is external. If they are employees, the demonstration is an internal talk and the authority would be write_internal. The time stays either way.
Focal upkeep is zero. No list or mapping is kept.
unknowns: Whether participants are patients or staff.
Whether she already keeps a written cue for the demonstration. This design does not add one.
research_questions: Does she keep any written cue for the demonstration, or is the session only spoken and shown?

already_counted.description: Reading the limits, choosing the routine, and demonstrating it stay in her week.

incremental.description: No list is kept. The demonstration uses limits already in the record.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The demonstration, the routine choice, and the limit check all stay. There is no second writing and no transport, so the low and the high are both zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prescribe the program and name the equipment in the record.

steps.what: Read limits, goals, and the last session in the clinical record {OTHER}
Prescribe individualized exercise programs, specifying equipment: treadmill, bicycle, ergometers, or perceptual goggles
Write that equipment list into the clinical record {OTHER}
Tell the participant the program while still in the room

tasks.design: She reads the clinical record {OTHER}, prescribes the program, and writes the equipment she is specifying into that same record. That writing is the prescription, so it stays. No work is removed. There is no second entry and no transport. Telling the person in the room stays. A machine does not prescribe.
tasks.previous_blocker: The program is a prescription. A draft is not one.
tasks.enabler_now: She still prescribes. No second copy is assumed, so nothing is removed.
tasks.still_hard: Matching load to a person who may be harmed by the wrong dose.
tasks.human_edge: She knows which equipment this person can use today.
tasks.altitude: She still prescribes the program, writes it in the record, and tells the person. Nothing in this task is removed.

reach.learn: How a physician records a load change the physiologist must not rewrite.

evidence.claim: A prescription comes from a named practitioner. AI drafts, it does not prescribe. She prescribes this program herself.
The program she writes in the clinical record is the prescription itself. Saving that same record is not a second writing.
A solely automated decision on care is restricted. She sets the program herself, so this design does not make one.

assumptions: The focal role is the exercise physiologist. The workflow boundary is this prescription: read the record, prescribe, write the equipment into that same record, tell the person. No other role's hours are in the baseline.
No structured input is produced for a machine. There is no machine step and no draft of the prescription.
No work is removed. The record write is the prescription, not a duplicate file. There is no second entry and no transport. A paper copy for the person is not assumed.
Participants are patients, outside the organisation, so telling them the program is external. If they are employees, that tell is an internal talk. The time stays either way.
Focal upkeep is zero. She does not keep a separate equipment list.
unknowns: Whether she also retypes the program onto something the person takes home. This design does not count a copy that may not exist.
Whether participants are patients or staff.
research_questions: Does she write the program only in the clinical record, or does she also retype it onto something the person takes home?

already_counted.description: Reading the record, prescribing, writing the equipment list, and telling the person stay in her week.

incremental.description: No second list is kept. She writes the program in the record she already uses.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Prescribing, writing the program in the same record, and telling the person all stay. There is no second writing and no transport, so the low and the high are both zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Judge progress after two named minute figures are subtracted.

steps.what: Read logged minutes and the target in the clinical record {OTHER}
Name the target minutes and the logged minutes to compare
Subtract the logged minutes from the target she named
Interpret exercise program participant data to evaluate progress or identify needed changes

tasks.design: The work removed is the hand subtraction of logged minutes from a target she named, and only that. She reads the session log in the clinical record {OTHER}, then names the two figures. The difference is computed only after that pair exists. It is not written back into the record as a separate saving. She still decides whether the program should change. Whoever first logged the minutes is outside this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress is a judgement. A difference of two minute figures is not that judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Once she names the target minutes and the logged minutes, subtracting them is arithmetic.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding whether a shortfall means the program should change.
tasks.human_edge: She can tell a missed session from a program that is too hard.
tasks.altitude: She still reads the log and still decides the program change. The only work removed is subtracting two minute figures she named.

reach.task: Compare logged practice minutes with a goal
reach.learn: Which two figures they treat as the comparison, and which judgement they keep.

evidence.claim: Subtracting a logged minute count from a target she named is arithmetic a short program can do once both numbers exist.
Health data are a special category, so a data-protection assessment is expected before the two minute fields are read for this subtraction. The session is not recorded.

assumptions: The focal role is the exercise physiologist. The workflow boundary is this review: read the log, name two figures, subtract them, decide the program change. The person who logged the minutes is outside her baseline.
The subtraction needs two fields she names in s2: target minutes and logged minutes. If either number is missing, the subtraction does not run and she judges from the log alone.
The work removed is only that hand subtraction. Storing the difference in the same clinical record {OTHER} is not counted. Nothing is sent.
One focal hour per 100 baseline hours confirms the two field names when the record layout changes. That hour is new.
If she never subtracts by hand and only looks at the log, the cut is zero.
unknowns: Whether she subtracts those two figures by hand today, or only reads the log.
Whether target minutes and logged minutes are already fields, or only prose in the note.
research_questions: Does she subtract logged minutes from a target by hand, or does she only look at the log?

already_counted.description: Reading the log, naming the two figures, and deciding the program change stay in her week.

incremental.description: She confirms the field names target minutes and logged minutes when the record layout changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A week where she always names both minute figures and always subtracts them by hand is the high case, after the hour that keeps the field names. A week where she only looks at the log has no subtraction to remove.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Recommend lifestyle activity from sentences she accepts.

steps.what: List the methods she will recommend and name one {DOCS} paragraph
Draft lifestyle sentences limited to her listed methods and that paragraph

loop.input: Her method list and the paragraph id she named.
loop.output: Sentences that cite that paragraph and add no method or number outside her list.
loop.check: A sentence that names a method or a minute target absent from her list fails.
loop.stop: One draft, or a second if the first fails. If the second fails, she speaks without the draft.
loop.why_not_simpler: A stored paragraph cannot tell whether a sentence added a method she did not list.

steps.what: Reject a sentence that adds a method or a number she did not list
Recommend methods to increase lifestyle physical activity

tasks.design: The work removed is drafting sentences limited to methods she listed and one vetted paragraph she named in {DOCS}. She lists the methods and names the paragraph first. She rejects a sentence that adds a method or a number. She still speaks the recommendation. Nothing is sent, and the sentences are not saved back as a separate cut. The conversation is not recorded. This is not a chatbot.
tasks.previous_blocker: Lifestyle advice has to stay inside methods she chooses, and a stored paragraph cannot know that.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can use only her method list and one paragraph she names, then she rejects anything extra.
tasks.still_hard: Saying the advice so this person can actually change the week.
tasks.human_edge: She hears what this person will not do and drops that method.
tasks.altitude: She still chooses the methods and still speaks the recommendation. The only work removed is drafting sentences from a paragraph she named.

reach.task: Tie a lifestyle line to a cited paragraph
reach.learn: Which paragraph ids the clinic allows a clinician to name.

evidence.claim: Thuisarts publishes guideline-based patient-education texts a clinician can cite.
Personal advice still needs her to accept the sentences before she says them. The spoken recommendation is not the sentence draft.
A chatbot that advises a patient must disclose that it is AI from 2 August 2026. This design is not a chatbot.
Works-council consent applies to ambient recording of how staff work. This design does not record the conversation.

assumptions: The focal role is the exercise physiologist. The workflow boundary is this recommendation: list methods, name a paragraph, draft sentences, reject a bad sentence, speak. A colleague who keeps paragraph ids is outside her baseline.
The draft needs two fields she produces in s1: a method list and a paragraph id from {DOCS}. If either is missing, the draft does not run and she speaks from memory.
A sentence that adds a method or a number outside her list is rejected. The check is about that meaning, not about an id match.
The work removed is only that sentence draft. Nothing is sent. Saving the sentences into the same store is not counted. The spoken recommendation stays.

A colleague keeps the ids of vetted paragraphs she may name. That is one other-role hour per 100 baseline hours and is not deducted from her net. Her own upkeep is zero because naming the paragraph is already inside s1.
Participants are patients, outside the organisation, so the spoken recommendation is external. If they are employees, it is an internal talk. The time stays either way.
If she speaks from memory and never writes the sentences, the draft replaces nothing.
unknowns: Which vetted paragraphs the organisation allows her to name.
Whether participants are patients or staff.
research_questions: Which vetted paragraphs is she allowed to name, and does she write the sentences before she speaks?

already_counted.description: Listing methods, rejecting a bad sentence, and speaking the recommendation stay in her week.

incremental.description: Naming the paragraph is already inside s1. She does not keep the paragraph list.
A colleague keeps the ids of vetted paragraphs she may name.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A week where she always lists methods, names a paragraph, and writes the sentences before she speaks is the high case. A week where she speaks from memory has no draft to remove. The colleague's paragraph list is not her time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still demonstrates, prescribes, interprets, and recommends. The only work removed is a hand subtraction of two minute figures and a lifestyle sentence draft she checks. Writing the program in the record stays.
reach: A physical therapist's home-exercise instruction, and how a dose change is written in the record.
How a dietitian ties a lifestyle line to a cited paragraph.
skills_to_grow: Name the target minutes and the logged minutes before a difference is computed.
Reject a drafted lifestyle sentence that adds a method or a number she did not list.
role.ambitious_version: No program is issued that she did not prescribe, and no sentence adds a method she did not list.
